key_insight: Structured EHR data can predict some depression and anxiety change in MS, but most of the signal comes from baseline severity and only modestly captures future trajectories.
clinical_relevance: This suggests clinicians should treat EHR-based mental health predictions as supportive context, not as a standalone tool for individual prognosis in multiple sclerosis.
method: Gradient boosting models were trained to predict PHQ-9 and GAD-7 score change.
Used longitudinal structured EHR data from MS patients with repeated observations.
Compared feature importance across depression and anxiety models.
evidence_signal: The models achieved modest performance, with R2 of 0.22 for PHQ-9 and 0.28 for GAD-7, indicating limited but measurable predictive signal.
watch_item: Predictions are heavily driven by baseline score and may reflect regression to the mean, so real-world use could overstate individual-level certainty.
paper_title: Predicting Depression and Anxiety Progression in Multiple Sclerosis from Longitudinal Clinical Data Using Machine Learning
